title.narrative: Transforming Inland Fisheries and Aquaculture in Kazakhstan to Ensure Environmental Sustainability

description.narrative: E.1 Knowledge management and Communication112. During the project inception phase, a knowledge management, communication and outreach strategy will be developed to promote engagement, share knowledge, experiences and project results (Activity 4.1; Budget: USD 106 894). The objective of the strategy will be to ensure that the knowledge assets generated through the project are made available and effectively disseminated to all stakeholders. This will not only require close engagement and coordination with producers and other actors in the value chain, but also with local, provincial and national authorities. The project’s aim to strengthen governance and management frameworks and to provide technical training and facilitate access to novel production systems and practices will amongst others, require knowledge sharing through local and national seminars, the recording and dissemination of project achievements, knowledge, and best practice cases studies, and the production of newsletters, news reports, videos and other media. The outreach strategy will focus on engaging with existing farmers, farmer associations and business fora to disseminate information on improved aquaculture practices, and to provide on-farm training demonstrations. Engagement with private sector support businesses (e.g. feed companies, hatcheries, and fish processors) will be supported through roundtables, and a media strategy will be developed to inform the wider public about benefits of sustainable aquaculture.113. Overseas technical exchange and training visits and cooperation with international experts, will be used to establish strategic institutional partnerships, and provide opportunities to share professional knowledge, technologies, and best practice. The active dissemination of the knowledge products through the CACFish work programme, will provide an important opportunity to share results and experiences with countries across the Central Asian and Caucus region – many of which are experiencing similar developmental issues to those currently prevalent in Kazakhstan. 114. Participation with the Food Systems Global Coordination Platform of the GEF Global Food System Integrated Programme (FSIP), and in particular collaboration with the cluster of countries that are targeting aquaculture development (South Africa, Namibia, Nigeria, Angola, Burkina Faso, Tanzania, Ghana, Kenya, China, and India) will ensure effective dissemination of key findings and results and contribute to the collection of global best practices and lessons learned. Participation will be sought in training and technical working groups and events organized by the Global Coordination Platform (GCP). Collaboration with the programme will build global expertise and contribute expertise to the global program.115. In addition, the program will leverage global and regional platforms as knowledge hubs to share lessons and to maximize stakeholder engagement. These include: · FAO's Committee on Fisheries (COFI) and its sub-committees, including but not limited to aquaculture and trade. · FAO's Committee on Food Security (CFS). · The Central Asian and Caucasus Regional Fisheries and Aquaculture Commission (CACFish).· Tehran Convention- Protection of the Marine Environment of the Caspian Sea · Eurasian Economic Union (EEU)E.2 Socio-economic Benefits and Decent Rural Employment [6]116. The project focuses on developing an enabling environment for aquaculture and culture based fisheries sector development will stimulate the establishment of small- and medium-scale companies, create employment opportunities and increase incomes in rural areas of Jetisu and Almaty Oblasts. Following the wider-scale dissemination of the production models and business cases, the emergence of new business enterprises is anticipated to expand to other regions throughout the country, providing further employment and income generating opportunities, and supporting resilience, food security and improved livelihoods for rural communities.117. FAO supports the Decent Work Agenda through the four pillars for Decent Rural Employment (DRE) framework. To this end, the project, supports the following pillars: Pillar 1 – employment creation and enterprise development – male and female small-scale producers supported in accessing markets and modern value chains; agribusiness and marketing micro, small and medium enterprises supported in accessing markets, training, financial services and other productive assets; vocational and educational training programmes on technical and business skills for rural people supported.Pillar 2 – Social protection: occupational safety and health measures for the rural workforce adopted by promoting safer technologies for small scale and commercial agriculture in extension programmes; working conditions improved in rural areas.Pillar 3 – Standards and rights at work: Socially responsible agricultural production supported, specifically to reduce gender and age-based discrimination.Pillar 4 – Governance and Social Dialogue: Countries supported in strengthening democratic organizations and networks of producers and workers, particularly in the informal rural food economy; Representation of the rural poor in social dialogue and policy dialogue, supported through their organizations; Participation of the rural poor in local decision-making and governance mechanisms supported; Rural women and youth groups empowered to be involved in these processes from the initial steps; Synergies built between organizations, programmes, countries and producer-to-producer learning opportunities created. [6] Specific guidance on how FAO can promote the Four Pillars of Decent Work in rural areas is provided in the Quick reference for addressing decent rural employment (as well as in the full corresponding Guidance document). For more information on FAO’s work on decent rural employment and related guidance materials please consult the FAO thematic website at: http://www.fao.org/rural-employment/en/.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Project Objective: Contribute towards the goals of the Kazakhstan Fisheries Development Programme (2021-2030) in support of transformation towards an environmentally friendly, climate resilient aquatic food systems
Indicator Targets: Core Indicator 4: Area of landscapes under improved practices - 28 121 ha Core Indicator 5.1: third-party certification that incorporates biodiversity considerations (number) - 1 MSC certified fishery Core Indicator 6: Greenhouse gas emissions mitigated - 450,347 metric tons CO2-eq Core Indicator 11: People benefiting from GEF-financed investments disaggregated by sex - 9,604 people (4,802 women)
